previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with a complex history of sclerosing mesenteritis, gastroparesis, and G-tube dependence was admitted for failure to thrive, persistent nausea, vomiting, and abdominal pain following discontinuation of home TPN due to insurance issues. She had lost 32 pounds and presented with malnutrition and hypocalcemia. During the 12-day admission, her G-tube was initially replaced to improve venting, but due to ongoing low output, it was subsequently changed to a Wills-Ogelsby tube, which improved drainage. A tunneled femoral central line was placed to reinitiate TPN after insurance approval. Nausea was managed with octreotide, ondansetron, and ativan, while dronabinol was discontinued due to sedation. Chronic pain remained stable on home medications. She was monitored for infection with negative blood and stool cultures. Upon discharge, she was stable on nightly TPN, with plans for weekly chem-10 monitoring, visiting nurse support, and follow-up with her care team.

radiology_notes.text:
INDICATION:  ___ female with a venting gastric tube which is not
adequately draining.  She has had many different gastric tubes placed recently
and the concern is that none have worked as well as her previous 12 ___
___ tube.  The patient understands that if replacing this tube does
not improve her venting of her stomach, they may have to investigate other
treatment routes for her nausea and abdominal pain.

PHYSICIAN:  ___, M.D., fellow, performed the procedure.  ___
___, M.D., attending, was supervising key portions of the procedure.

FLUOROSCOPY TIME:  40 seconds.

MEDICATIONS:  Moderate sedation was provided by administering divided doses of
fentanyl totalling 75 mcg and Versed totalling 1 mg throughout the total
intraservice time of 25 minutes during which the patient's hemodynamic
parameters were continuously monitored.

PROCEDURE:  Percutaneous G-tube exchange.

PROCEDURE DETAILS:  Informed consent was obtained from the patient.  She was
positioned supine.  The area was prepped and draped in sterile fashion.  A
timeout was performed.  Fluoroscopy was used intermittently.

We first injected some contrast into the indwelling tube, showing the patient
the spot image and explaining to her that the stomach appeared quite empty at
the start of the procedure.  We agreed to continue with the tube exchange. 
The patient had a modified 14 ___ ___ with the tip shortened and
multiple additional sideholes cut.  Per discussion with the patient and the
referring team, we were to replace this back with a 12 ___ ___
tube.  A ___ wire was advanced through the indwelling tube to coil within
the stomach.  The indwelling tube was removed, and a new 12 ___
___ tube was advanced into the stomach.  The wire was removed.  The
pigtail was formed.  The catheter was affixed to the skin with suture.  A
purse-string suture was also placed given the size mismatch.  Final position
was demonstrated with a contrast injection. There were no complications.

FINDINGS:  Nondistended stomach at the start of the procedure.

CONCLUSION:  Uncomplicated exchange of percutaneous gastric tube, the patient
now has a 12 ___ ___ gastric tube.

STUDY:  Abdomen supine and erect films ___.  

CLINICAL HISTORY:  ___ woman with history of bowel obstruction, now
with increased vomiting.

FINDINGS:  There are a few pockets of gas seen within the colon.  No definite
dilated loops of small bowel are seen.  The amount of air in the bowel has
decreased from prior.  A nephrostomy tube on the left side is seen.  There is
also a left-sided catheter within the pelvis.  Overall, this bowel gas pattern
is non-obstructive.  There is stool in the rectum and sigmoid colon.  There
are degenerative changes of the lower lumbar spine and bilateral hip joints. 
There is no free intra-abdominal gas.
